candidates.explanation: After verifying the reset hash, the password is updated but existing sessions are never invalidated. The upstream boilerplate calls sessionService.deleteByUserId({ userId: user.id }) after updating the password. Without it, previously issued refresh tokens/sessions stay valid, so an already signed-in device can keep refreshing its login.

Updating the password here does not revoke the user's sessions, so a password change through this path leaves existing refresh sessions active. This is secondary, since the caller should handle session revocation.

fix.description: In AuthService.resetPassword, after `await this.usersService.update(user.id, user)`, delete all of the user's sessions with `await this.sessionService.deleteByUserId({ userId: user.id })`. This makes every device sign in again, and refresh tokens fail validation. Inject SessionService if it isn't already injected.
